title: Multiregion TLS Handshake Failure - Operator Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures triage notes, temporary mitigations, and an operator playbook template for region-level TLS handshake degradations that cause traffic to rehome across regions. It is a working playbook (draft) — intended for on-call SREs, Edge/LoadBalancer owners, and Platform network engineers.

Background summary (incident observed 2025-02-13):
- At ~09:12 UTC we started to see elevated TLS handshake latency and client-side connection timeouts originating from clients routed to region-eu-west-1 edge cluster.
- Symptoms: increased SYN->TLS handshake duration, TLS retransmits, occasional handshake aborts (TLS alerts), followed by client SDK re-resolves and falling back to other regions causing bursty traffic in us-west-2 and ap-southeast-1.
- Impact: 8–12% request error rate for chat/generate endpoints for EU customers for ~48 minutes; downstream spikes in backend CPU and KV-cache miss rates in fallback regions.

Quick detection signals (use these first):
- Edge metrics: tls_handshake_ms (p95/p99), tls_alert_count, connection_reset_rate per edge-pop/region
- LB health: upstream healthcheck failures, backend connection queue length
- DNS: sudden increase in resolver retries/timeout counts from our authoritative DNS logs; TTL compliance telemetry (client re-resolve frequency)
- Client telemetry: SDK reconnects, fallback-region selection logs
- Infra: TLS offload node CPU and process restart traces

Hypotheses (what tends to cause this class of incident):
1) Certificate chain or OCSP/CRL latency problems at the edge (OCSP responder unreachable or slow).
2) TLS library/kernel regressions introduced in a recent edge rollout (e.g., renegotiation or SNI parsing change).
3) Network path MTU or middlebox interfering with handshake (fragmentation causing retransmits).
4) Resource exhaustion on edge TLS worker threads (file descriptors, L4 ephemeral port exhaustion).
5) Upstream CA rotation or misconfigured cert bundles deployed to subset of edge pool.

Mitigations attempted during the incident (notes on what we tried):
- 09:18 UTC: Bounced TLS offload workers on a subset of affected pops -> partial reduction in error rate but not complete.
- 09:25 UTC: Temporarily increased edge LB capacity (scale up) to reduce queueing; handshakes still slow.
- 09:32 UTC: Rolled back latest edge cert bundle to previous stable on 3 of 5 affected clusters -> immediate p50 handshake improvement in those clusters.
- 09:40 UTC: Reduced authoritative DNS TTL from 60s to 10s for affected CNAMEs to speed client re-resolve (helps rehome away from broken nodes) — risky but useful for mitigation.
- 09:48 UTC: Enabled graceful connection drain on flagged edge nodes and moved traffic via weighted routing to healthy regions.

What worked / tradeoffs observed: 
- Rolling back cert bundle produced the clearest improvement where that bundle had been applied. Indicates config/certging problem rather than pure network.
- TTL drop accelerated client movement but caused heavier churn and more cache-miss load in downstream services; used only as short-term emergency lever.
- Bouncing processes helped some nodes but increased transient failures for in-flight sessions; use as last resort for isolated nodes.

Operator Playbook (step-by-step) — concise checklist for an on-call SRE:
1) Initial assessment (first 5–10 minutes)
   - Confirm scope: check p95/p99 tls_handshake latency by region/pop, and client error-rate dashboards.
   - Query authoritative DNS logs for resolver timeout spikes and client re-resolve counts.
   - Check deployment history for any edge config/cert/library rollouts in the last 2 hours (k8s/edge-image deploys, cert push pipelines).

2) Immediate containment (10–25 minutes)
   - If cert bundle was recently pushed: trigger a targeted rollback to previous bundle on a canary pop and observe handshake metrics.
   - If no cert change, check OCSP/OCSP stapling telemetry and OCSP responder health; if OCSP is failing, temporarily disable stapling on affected edge cluster (note: security tradeoff) OR configure cached stapling responses if available.
   - If edge nodes show thread/FD exhaustion: enable extra worker threads or drain/recycle the affected hosts. Avoid mass recycle unless confirmed.

3) Traffic steering (25–45 minutes)
   - Prefer weighted-region rehoming over DNS TTL changes where possible. Update traffic weights in Steering service to shift ~25% increments and observe.
   - If steering is ineffective and immediate offload is required, reduce DNS TTL to 10s for affected CNAMEs, but prepare rollback and scale downstream caches/backends.
   - Enable connection draining on problem hosts before removing them from rotation to reduce TLS aborts for in-flight sessions.

4) Verification and stabilization (45–120 minutes)
   - Watch p50/p95/p99 handshake latency and tls_alert counts for at least two handshake windows (~minutes).
   - Monitor backend CPU, request latency, KV-cache hit-rate for fallback regions to detect secondary overload.
   - If traffic has rehomed, plan gradual traffic re-convergence with staging and canary validations.

5) Rollback and remediation (post-stable)
   - Keep rollback of suspect artifact until root cause confirmed.
   - Collect full evidence: edge logs, pack traces of failing handshakes, packet captures for sample clients (pcap), config diffs.
   - Open follow-up JIRA with owner, attach artifacts and timeline.

Quick commands & locations (notes to self):
- Edge metrics query (Grafana): row SRE > edge-pop > tls_handshake_ms{pop=~"eu-.*"}
- LB control plane: kubectl -n edge rollout status deploy/edge-terminator-<pop>
- Auth DNS logs: /var/log/dns-auth/resolve-events (or DNS-telemetry dashboard)
- OCSP probe: internal/ocsp-probe service -> health check endpoint
- TLS worker stats: /api/edge/metrics/worker-stats (requires SRE token)

Smoke tests (post-fix validation):
- From 3 vantage points (eu vm, us vm, ap vm): run s_client openssl handshake to edge-host, record time to handshake and certificate chain.
- Synthetic user flow through SDK for generate/chat with 5 concurrent sessions for 2 minutes to ensure no 5xx regressions.
- Validate OCSP stapling content via curl -v --tls-max 1.3 and inspect stapled response.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did only subset of pops get the bad cert bundle? Investigate rollout pipeline (rolling window/payment?).
- Are our OCSP responder redundancies adequate from all edge regions? Add synthetic checks from each region.
- Should we add automatic gating to cert-bundle deployment if handshake p99 increases by >X ms in canary?
- Investigate client SDK behavior: aggressive re-resolve vs. retry logic is amplifying impact — propose soft-fallback delay to avoid cascade.

Post-incident action items (owners & rough ETA):
- SRE: Add TLS handshake canary alert (p99 increase) and automatic rollback runbook (owner: Ethan, ETA: 2w).
- Edge infra: Harden cert bundle rollout with extra validation and region-level dry-run flags (owner: María, ETA: 3w).
- Networking: Add regional OCSP responder probes and fallback caches (owner: Samir, ETA: 4w).
- SDK: Add jittered re-resolve/backoff on region-failover in SDK (owner: client-sdk team, ETA: 6w).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and includes risky emergency levers (TTL squeeze, disabling stapling temporarily). Each emergency lever must be approved in-call by senior SRE or infra lead before execution. Please annotate any missing CLI steps or dashboards I should add.

Raw timeline notes (operator timestamps):
- 09:12 start: first alarm (p99 tls_handshake ms up)
- 09:18: process bounce attempt on pop-eu-3
- 09:25: scale up edge LB on eu cluster
- 09:32: rollback cert-bundle on pop-eu-2/3/4 -> improvement observed
- 09:40: TTL lowered to 10s for affected CNAMEs (emergency)
- 10:00: traffic steering weights adjusted to offload 60% to us-west-2
- 10:40: steady state restored, metrics trending nominal

Endnotes: keep this file as a mutable working playbook. If you execute any step, append a short note with time and outcome. We'll converge this into a formal runbook after 1–2 postmortem sessions.

-- Aisha
